## Data availability

This study used individual-level phenotypic and DNA methylation data from participants in the AGES-Reykjavik Study, with tiered access provided to protect participant privacy. Complete individual-level data and detailed demographic information are restricted to approved collaborators who have executed formal Data Use Agreements with the Principal Investigator and relevant institutional authorities; additional data files requiring controlled access can be obtained upon reasonable request to the corresponding author, subject to appropriate data use agreements and institutional review board approval. Processed summary statistics and derived data files [are publicly available in the project's GitHub repository [@RN105]]{.rev}, under `data/publicly_available/` and released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. Association data for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) and the Australian Imaging, Biomarkers, and Lifestyle (AIBL) studies, along with meta-analysis results, were obtained from the MIAMI-AD database [@RN82]. Association data for the AddNeuroMed cohort were downloaded from the supplementary data of the reference [@RN24].

## Code availability

All analysis code [is publicly available in the same GitHub repository [@RN105]]{.rev}. The repository includes documentation, analysis scripts, and visualization code, organized by analysis section to allow researchers to run specific components or the complete pipeline. All analyses are fully reproducible using the provided code and the instructions in the repository README, provided data access is granted (see Data availability). Analyses were performed in R (version 4.5.2), with all analysis documents written in Quarto; the full list of package versions is given in the Methods. The variational autoencoder was implemented in R using keras3 with the TensorFlow backend. The complete pipeline is rebuilt through the orchestration script `manage_project/render_manuscript.sh`.

## Disclosure

Artificial intelligence tools were used to assist with manuscript writing, including grammar and language improvement, and to support coding tasks during the analysis pipeline development. [A large language model also assisted in selecting the keywords that assign Gene Ontology terms to the author-defined functional categories (see Methods).]{.rev} All AI-assisted content was carefully reviewed and validated by the authors.
